qe: The difference between the selling price and the cost price of an item is ₹360. If the profit is 20%, what is the cost price (in ₹)?
qh: एक वस्तु के विक्रय मूल्य और क्रय मूल्य के बीच का अंतर ₹360 है। यदि लाभ 20% है, तो क्रय मूल्य (₹ में) क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Step 1: Profit% = 20% = 1/5.
Step 2: Denominator = CP = 5 units, Numerator = Profit = 1 unit.
SP = CP + Profit = 5 + 1 = 6 units.
Difference between SP and CP = SP - CP = Profit = 1 unit.
Step 3: Question ke anusar, 1 unit = ₹360.
Step 4: CP = 5 units = 5 * 360 = ₹1,800.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹1800 hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Step 1: Mana CP = 100%.
Step 2: SP - CP = Profit = 20%.
Step 3: 20% = ₹360 ==> 1% = 360 / 20 = 18.
Step 4: CP (100%) = 100 * 18 = ₹1,800.
Atah sahi uttar '₹1800' hai.

Exam point: labh-haani ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: A shopkeeper sold an article at a 26% profit. On selling it for ₹2,250 more, he would get a profit of 41%. If this article is sold at 12% profit, then the selling price would be:
qh: एक दुकानदार ने एक वस्तु 26% के लाभ पर बेची। इसे ₹2,250 अधिक में बेचने पर उसे 41% का लाभ प्राप्त होता। यदि यह वस्तु 12% के लाभ पर बेची जाती है, तो विक्रय मूल्य क्या होगा?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Step 1: Profit badhne ka antar = 41% - 26% = 15%.
15% = 3/20.
Step 2: Base CP = 20 units, Increase = 3 units.
Question ke anusar, 3 units = ₹2,250 ==> 1 unit = 2250 / 3 = ₹750.
CP = 20 units = 20 * 750 = ₹15,000.
Step 3: Naya profit = 12% = 3/25.
CP : Naya SP = 25 : (25 + 3) = 25 : 28.
25 units = 15,000 ==> 1 unit = 600.
Naya SP = 28 units = 28 * 600 = ₹16,800.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹16,800 hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Step 1: Mana CP = 100%.
Step 2: SP1 = 126%, SP2 = 141%.
Difference = 141% - 126% = 15%.
Step 3: 15% = ₹2,250 ==> 1% = 2250 / 15 = 150.
Step 4: 12% labh par SP = 112% = 112 * 150 = ₹16,800.
Atah sahi uttar '₹16,800' hai.

Exam point: labh-haani ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: A trader sells an article at 16% below its cost price. Had he sold it for ₹192.20 more, he would have gained 15%. The new selling price (in ₹) of the article is:
qh: एक व्यापारी एक वस्तु को उसके क्रय मूल्य से 16% कम पर बेचता है। यदि उसने इसे ₹192.20 अधिक में बेचा होता, तो उसे 15% का लाभ होता। वस्तु का नया विक्रय मूल्य (₹ में) क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Step 1: Loss = 16%, Gain = 15%.
Kul badlav = 16% + 15% = 31%.
31% = 31/100.
Step 2: Base CP = 100 units, Difference = 31 units.
Question ke anusar, 31 units = ₹192.20 ==> 1 unit = 192.20 / 31 = ₹6.20.
Step 3: Naya SP (15% profit par) = CP + 15% = 100 + 15 = 115 units.
Step 4: Naya SP = 115 units = 115 * 6.20 = ₹713.
Atah sahi vikalp  713 hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Step 1: Mana CP = 100%.
Step 2: SP1 = 100% - 16% = 84%.
SP2 = 100% + 15% = 115%.
Antar = 115% - 84% = 31%.
Step 3: 31% = ₹192.20 ==> 1% = 192.20 / 31 = 6.20.
Step 4: Naya SP = 115% = 115 * 6.20 = ₹713.
Atah sahi uttar '713' hai.

Exam point: diye gaye tathyon ka sahi milan - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: A man sold his cycle at 17% loss. If he had sold it for 1,056 more, he would have made 5% profit. The cost price of the cycle is:
qh: एक व्यक्ति ने अपनी साइकिल 17% की हानि पर बेची। यदि उसने इसे 1,056 अधिक में बेचा होता, तो उसे 5% का लाभ प्राप्त होता। साइकिल का क्रय मूल्य है:
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Step 1: Loss = 17%, Profit = 5%.
Kul badlav = 17% + 5% = 22%.
22% = 22/100 = 11/50.
Step 2: Base CP = 50 units, Value badhne ka antar = 11 units.
Question ke anusar, 11 units = ₹1,056 ==> 1 unit = 1056 / 11 = ₹96.
Step 3: CP = 50 units = 50 * 96 = ₹4,800.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹4,800 hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Step 1: Mana CP = 100%.
Step 2: SP1 = 100% - 17% = 83%.
SP2 = 100% + 5% = 105%.
Antar = 105% - 83% = 22%.
Step 3: 22% = ₹1,056 ==> 1% = 1056 / 22 = 48.
Step 4: CP (100%) = 100 * 48 = ₹4,800.
Atah sahi uttar '₹4,800' hai.

Exam point: labh-haani ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: A seller sold a bag at a profit of 12%. If he had sold it for ₹900 more, he would have gained 27%. What is the CP of the bag?
qh: एक विक्रेता ने एक बैग 12% के लाभ पर बेचा। यदि उसने इसे ₹900 अधिक में बेचा होता, तो उसे 27% का लाभ होता। बैग का क्रय मूल्य क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Step 1: Profit badhne ka antar = 27% - 12% = 15%.
15% = 3/20.
Step 2: Base CP = 20 units, Antar = 3 units.
Question ke anusar, 3 units = ₹900 ==> 1 unit = 900 / 3 = ₹300.
Step 3: CP = 20 units = 20 * 300 = ₹6,000.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹6,000 hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Step 1: Mana CP = 100%.
Step 2: SP1 = 112%, SP2 = 127%.
Antar = 127% - 112% = 15%.
Step 3: 15% = ₹900 ==> 1% = 900 / 15 = 60.
Step 4: CP (100%) = 100 * 60 = ₹6,000.
Atah sahi uttar '₹6,000' hai.

Exam point: labh-haani ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.

qe: On selling a table for ₹210 and ₹420 there will be loss of L1% and L2% respectively. If L1 - L2 = 7, then what is the cost price of table?
qh: एक मेज को ₹210 और ₹420 में बेचने पर क्रमशः L1% और L2% की हानि होती है। यदि L1 - L2 = 7 है, तो मेज का क्रय मूल्य क्या है?
e:
Method 1 (Ratio Method):
Step 1: Dono vikray mulya (SP) ka antar = 420 - 210 = ₹210.
Step 2: Yeh antar loss% ke antar ke barabar hai: L1% - L2% = 7% of CP.
7% = 7/100.
Denominator = CP = 100 units, Numerator = Antar = 7 units.
Step 3: Question ke anusar, 7 units = ₹210 ==> 1 unit = 210 / 7 = ₹30.
Step 4: CP = 100 units = 100 * 30 = ₹3,000.
Atah sahi vikalp  ₹3,000 hai.

Method 2 (100-Base Method):
Step 1: Mana CP = 100%.
Step 2: Loss% ka antar = (SP2 - SP1) / CP * 100% = 7%.
Step 3: 7% of CP = 420 - 210 = ₹210.
1% of CP = 210 / 7 = 30.
Step 4: CP (100%) = 100 * 30 = ₹3,000.
Atah sahi uttar '₹3,000' hai.

Exam point: labh-haani ka niyam - ise yaad rakhein; isi tarah ke prashn pariksha mein doharaaye jaate hain.
